  In accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, if you require a disability-related
  modification or accommodation to attend or participate in this meeting, including auxiliary aids or services,

  Any disclosable public records related to an open session item on a regular meeting agenda and

  AGENDA
  Regular Meeting of the City Council
  CITY OF WESTLAKE VILLAGE
  City Council Chambers
  31200 Oak Crest Drive

  Wednesday, March 9, 2022 - 6:30 p.m.

  Written comments may be sent to the City Clerk's Office at antoinette@wlv.org no later than
  12:00 p.m. on Wednesday, March 9, 2022. Written comments will be summarized during the
  meeting.

  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION OPTIONS:

  The Public may join this meeting virtually or attend in-person in the Council Chambers. At the
  time of this agenda posting, for the Public to attend in person, all vaccinated individuals must
  show proof of vaccination and ID to participate indoors without wearing a mask. Individuals
  without proof of vaccination and ID will be asked to wear a mask.

  Due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, City Council members and staff may be participating
  in this meeting via teleconference pursuant to Government Code Section 54953(e).

  Please click the link below to join the webinar:

PUBLIC COMMENTS:

Natalie Garber, Westlake Village, introduced her new business, Hummus Lali, located in
the Shoppes at Westlake Village.

Dr. Denise Danne, Westlake Village, apprised of New West Symphony "New to You"
Marketplace event, to be held on March 12, 2022 - 9:00 am - 3:00 pm at the Westlake
Village City Hall Courtyard. She encouraged residents to come out and support the event
whose proceeds will benefit music in the elementary schools.

STAFF COMMENTS:

City Manager de Geus welcomed City Councilmembers back to in-person meetings in the
City Council Chambers, stating it has been a long journey with COVID-19 restrictions and
mandates for our community, staff, and City Council, throughout the past two years. He
noted that he was looking forward to the year ahead with everyone back in the Council
Chambers.

City Manager de Geus introduced Lieutenant Joe Fender as the Acting Captain for the
Lost Hills Sheriffs Station, stating Captain Becerra was reassigned to the Norwalk
Station. City Manager de Geus stated Westlake Village is fortunate to be working again
with Acting Captain Fender, having already demonstrated his responsiveness and
commitment to the City, in supporting public safety for our residents and businesses.

Acting Captain Fender stated that he was humbled to be back with Westlake Village. He
reminded residents that prior to this assignment, he served as Detective Lieutenant for a
year, moving to become the Operations Lieutenant for the North Patrol Division, then the
Personal Aide for the Captain for eight months.

  1.  ASSEMBLY BILL {AB) 361 FINDINGS FOR SPECIAL BROWN ACT
  REQUIREMENTS FOR TELECONFERENCE MEETINGS

  City Manager de Geus introduced the item and requested the City Council approve
  findings that will continue to allow for the option of virtual meetings for City Council
  and Committee meetings. Findings must be made every 30 days. He noted that
  while staff is recommending these findings, the intent is to continue with in-person
  City Council meetings barring any changes in COVID-19 over the next 30 days.

  Councilmember Honig moved to approve the City Council findings that
  teleconference meetings of the City Council and the City's committees can
  continue to be conducted pursuant to the AB 361 special Brown Act requirements:
  the City Council has reconsidered the circumstances of the COVID-19 state of

  promote social distancing. Councilmember Mcsweeney seconded the motion.

  2.  ZERO-EMISSIONS LANDSCAPING EQUIPMENT ORDINANCE UPDATE-

  City Manager de Geus introduced the item and Planning Director Forbes provided
  an update on the zero-emissions landscaping equipment ordinance noting that in
  November 2021, the City Council directed staff to move forward with transitioning
  City maintenance contracts to zero-emission equipment and to prepare an
  ordinance to prohibit gasoline powered landscape equipment.
   City Council Minutes
  City of Westlake Village  March 9, 2022  5

  OLD BUSINESS (continued):

l
  Mr. Forbes stated that two separate ordinances will be prepared: one for leaf
  blowers and one for other landscape equipment. Staff anticipated bringing the leaf
  blower ordinance to City Council this summer with the ordinance taking effect in
  January 2023 and the other landscape equipment ordinance this winter with the
  ordinance taking effect in July 2023. This will allow for public outreach and
  education as the second ordinance will affect the landscaping industry and
  property owners.

  Mr. Forbes noted that staff will be working with the American Green Zone Alliance
  related to public outreach and education on zero-emission landscape equipment.
  Twelve outreach meetings will be conducted, with one meeting planned each
  quarter for the various audience groups, starting now and continuing through the
  first quarter of 2023. Additional outreach will also be conducted via the website,
  social media, and newsletter to ensure the public and landscapers are aware of
  these changes.

  Dan Mabe, American Green Zone Alliance, addressed City Council questions on
  the landscaping industry moving to zero-emission equipment, federal/state funding
  to assist with moving to zero-emission equipment. Mr. Mabe stated that Assembly
  Bill 1346 provides some funding for landscaping businesses to transition to zero-
  emission equipment; however, determination is pending on whether the air quality
  districts will be the agencies that receive the funding and process the grants.

  The Council expressed concerns on the enforcement provision that will have a
  fiscal impact on the City. The Council's preference was to provide more incentives
  to encourage residents and property owners to make this change and encouraged
  staff to consider how the City might provide some form of assistance in this
  transition.

  Councilmember Honig moved to direct staff to proceed with the preparation of
  ordinances requiring use of zero-emissions landscaping equipment including
  public outreach and education as recommended by staff. Councilmember Davis
  seconded the motion.

  YES:  Councilmembers Mcsweeney, Honig, Davis, Mayor Pro Tern
  Pearl, Mayor Halpern.
